body.x: A brand that runs several social media channels spends much of its day on the same few tasks: reading comments, answering customer questions, replying to direct messages and filtering spam. The work grows with every channel and every data source, and it leaves less time for strategy.

Digitalog Technologies Inc., an IT company based in Yeoksam-dong, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, was founded to hand that work to AI. Led by CEO Alex Son, the company is taking part in FIX 2026 and was selected as a winner in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards.

According to Digitalog, Son has more than 10 years of marketing experience across Australia, Japan and Korea, including marketing and digital business roles at Google, General Mills and Criteo, and holds a master's degree from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST). The company says he returned to Korea during the COVID-19 pandemic and, comparing the practices of global companies with the fast-changing digital environment in Korea, became interested in changing corporate marketing through AI. In his own one-line definition, the company says, he solves the problem of automating repetitive, inefficient marketing and communication tasks with AI so that companies can communicate more effectively with fewer resources.

Digitalog describes itself as an IT company that helps organizations reach AI transformation (AX) and digital transformation (DX). It says it combines AI, data analytics, software and automation technologies, and that its approach goes beyond using generative AI to create content: it aims to understand how organizations actually work, connect the necessary data and systems, and let AI take part directly in business processes. The company says many marketing organizations still depend on manual, repetitive processes even though they have adopted advertising platforms, customer relationship management (CRM) systems, analytics tools and social media platforms, and that it started from that gap.

Its flagship service is Conma AI, an AI-powered social media automation service. Digitalog says it supports platforms such as Instagram and Facebook and offers comment management, customer inquiry collection, AI-powered comment responses, automated direct messages, and detection and management of spam and harmful comments. The company says it is developing Conma AI as an operational platform that connects AI directly to the workflows of businesses and brands, not as a content generation tool. It has also released Marcomm AI, which supports corporate public relations and marketing communications with AI-assisted press release creation, online newsroom management, Press CRM, competitor monitoring and social media monitoring.

On commercialization, Digitalog says full-scale development of Conma AI began in September 2025 and an initial beta version followed in November 2025. After about six months of beta operation with feedback and usage data from real users, paid service began in May 2026, and the company says registered users, paying customers and revenue have grown every month since. It says that releasing an early version and validating it with users let it find strong demand among influencers and small business owners that it had not anticipated. The company says roughly 80% of its registered users and paying customers are influencers and small business owners, which it takes as evidence that demand for social media automation is not limited to large companies. Its stated primary users are marketing professionals at enterprises and influencers and creators, across industries including automotive, fashion, beauty, retail, financial technology and food and beverage.

In Korea, Digitalog reports that Conma AI is used by organizations including Shinhan Bank, BNK Kyongnam Bank, NongHyup, SK Telecom, LG Uplus, Shinsegae Department Store, Sulbing, Harim, CU, T-money, Lotte Holdings, CJ Group, Hanwha Financial Plus and Lotte Rental, and by public-sector users such as the Mapo-gu Office, the Seongdong-gu Office, the Gyeonggi Tourism Organization and the Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture. It says a growing number have become paying customers and that it built its customer base without large paid marketing campaigns. The company has also been selected for AI startup support programs run by Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA and AWS, and has been named an official Meta Tech Provider and, more recently, a PwC AI Agent Connector.

The service has initial customers in eight countries: Korea, the U.S., Japan, Brazil, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia and Australia. Its current export markets, as the application lists them, are the U.S., Japan, Brazil, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand and Australia, and its stated difficulty is developing sales channels. Digitalog has named Vietnam, Thailand, Japan and the U.S. as priority markets, chosen for the size of social media and influencer marketing, demand for software as a service (SaaS), purchasing power for digital services and long-term expansion potential. In Vietnam and Thailand, it plans direct sales to influencers, creators and small businesses along with partnerships with local marketing agencies, technology companies and resellers. In Japan, where the company says its founder has firsthand experience, it plans to strengthen Japanese-language features and support and build partners and resellers. In the U.S., it plans to acquire customers first through online SaaS sales and later add business customers through local partnerships. The company says it will localize Conma AI for each market rather than export one product everywhere.

In Vietnam, the company says its first customers are mainly influencers, so it is pursuing corporate customers through the Shinhan Future's Lab program. It says it met Shinhan Bank Vietnam and that the two sides have confirmed a proof of concept (PoC), which Digitalog plans to use as a reference case for financial institutions' social media operations and customer communication, and then to approach other financial institutions, large companies, brands and midsize companies in Vietnam. In Thailand, it plans to start with direct SaaS sales and add corporate customers through local digital marketing agencies.

On the product side, Digitalog plans to evolve Conma AI from a social media management tool into a broader workflow automation platform, adding customer inquiry analysis, content operations, social media data analysis, marketing performance measurement and stronger multilingual support. It also plans to expand Marcomm AI, and to extend its relationships with Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, AWS, Meta and PwC into customer adoption, joint business development, reseller programs and enterprise AX and DX projects. Over time it aims to extend the model validated in Korea to Japan, Southeast Asia and the U.S., followed by other markets including Europe, and to raise the share of overseas revenue from recurring subscriptions.

Now in its third year, FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Technology Expo) is a future-industry exhibition that combines and connects innovative technologies in future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. It runs from Wednesday, Oct. 21, to Saturday, Oct. 24, at EXCO in Daegu. Under the theme "AI, Beyond Tech into Reality," the exhibition shares industry trends and core technologies through AI-based technology exhibitions, conferences and lectures by experts from Korea and abroad, and networking programs.
